name: Idli
steps: Soak rice and dal separately for 6 hours.
Grind dal to fluffy paste and rice to coarse batter.
Mix with salt and ferment for 8-12 hours.
Steam in idli plates for 10 minutes.

name: Dosa
steps: Grind soaked rice and dal into a very smooth batter.
Ferment for 8 hours until slightly bubbly.
Spread thin on a hot tawa and drizzle oil.
Cook until crisp and golden brown.

name: Ven Pongal
steps: Pressure cook rice and dal with 4 cups water per cup until mushy.
Temper ghee with pepper, cumin, ginger, and curry leaves.
Fold tempering and salt into the cooked rice-dal mix.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Rava Upma
steps: Dry roast rava until aromatic; set aside.
Temper mustard, urad dal, ginger, and chillies in oil.
Add water (1:2.5 ratio) and salt; bring to boil.
Stir in rava slowly and cook until water is absorbed.

name: Rava Dosa
steps: Mix flours with water to a very thin, watery consistency.
Add crushed pepper, cumin, ginger, and salt.
Pour batter from edges toward center on a hot tawa.
Drizzle oil and cook until lacey and crisp; do not flip.

name: Semiya Upma
steps: Roast vermicelli and set aside.
Temper mustard, urad dal, and chillies; sauté onions.
Add water (1:1.5 ratio), salt, and boil.
Add vermicelli and simmer until dry and fluffy.

name: Kuzhi Paniyaram
steps: Temper mustard, chana dal, and onions; mix into idli batter.
Grease paniyaram pan and fill holes with batter.
Cook until edges crisp, then flip with a stick.
Remove once both sides are golden brown.

name: Onion Uttapam
steps: Pour a thick ladle of batter on a hot tawa.
Top generously with chopped onions, chillies, and coriander.
Drizzle oil around edges and press onions lightly.
Flip and cook until onions are caramelized.

name: Idiyappam
steps: Mix rice flour with boiling water and salt into a soft dough.
Press through an idiyappam mold onto steamer plates.
Sprinkle grated coconut on top.
Steam for 5-7 minutes and serve with coconut milk.

name: Poori Kizhangu
steps: Knead wheat flour into a stiff dough and deep fry rolled circles.
Mash boiled potatoes roughly.
Sauté onions, ginger, and turmeric; mix with potatoes and water.
Simmer until gravy thickens and serve with fried pooris.

name: Masala Dosa
steps: Prepare a dry potato bhaji with onions and turmeric.
Spread dosa batter thinly; drizzle oil and cook until crisp.
Place potato masala in the center.
Fold the dosa over and serve with chutney.

name: Medhu Vadai
steps: Grind soaked dal with minimal water into a thick, fluffy batter.
Mix in salt, crushed pepper, ginger, and curry leaves.
Shape into donuts on a wet palm.
Deep fry until golden brown and crispy.

name: Aval Upma
steps: Rinse poha and drain water; let it soften.
Temper mustard, peanuts, and curry leaves in oil.
Sauté onions and turmeric; add softened poha and salt.
Toss gently and finish with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Ragi Dosa
steps: Whisk ragi, rice flour, and curd with water to a thin batter.
Add chopped onions, cumin, and salt.
Pour on a hot tawa and drizzle oil.
Cook both sides until the ragi darkens and crisps.

name: Ragi Kali
steps: Cook broken rice in excess water until very soft.
Mix ragi flour with water to a paste and add to the rice.
Stir vigorously without lumps until thick and cooked.
Shape into balls and serve with buttermilk or sambar.

name: Adai
steps: Soak rice and mixed dals for 4 hours; grind coarsely with chillies.
Add hing, salt, and chopped curry leaves to the thick batter.
Spread thick on a tawa; make a small hole in the center for oil.
Cook both sides until reddish-brown and crisp.

name: Bread Omelette
steps: Whisk eggs with onions, chillies, salt, and pepper.
Pour onto a hot tawa; place bread slices on the wet egg.
Flip the whole omelette so bread toasts on the tawa.
Fold the egg edges over the bread and serve.

name: Oats Upma
steps: Lightly toast oats and set aside.
Temper mustard and chillies; sauté vegetables with turmeric.
Add water (1:1.5 ratio) and salt; bring to boil.
Add oats and cook for 3 minutes until soft but not mushy.

name: Kambu Dosa
steps: Soak millet, rice, and dal; grind into a smooth batter.
Ferment overnight for 8-10 hours.
Spread thin on a tawa like a regular dosa.
Cook until golden; serve with spicy tomato chutney.

name: Set Dosa
steps: Grind soaked rice, dal, and poha into a smooth, airy batter.
Ferment for 10 hours.
Pour small, thick pancakes; do not spread.
Cook covered with a lid until porous and spongy.

name: Varagu Pongal
steps: Pressure cook millet and dal together until soft.
Temper ghee with crushed pepper, cumin, and curry leaves.
Mix tempering and salt into the millet mixture.
Serve as a healthy alternative to rice pongal.

name: Wheat Dosa (Godhumai)
steps: Mix wheat and rice flour with water into a thin, lump-free batter.
Add chopped onions, chillies, cumin, and salt.
Pour on a medium-hot tawa and drizzle oil.
Cook both sides until brown (this is an instant dosa).

name: Pesuaraittu (Sprouts) Dosa
steps: Grind sprouts with ginger, chilli, and cumin into a batter.
Add salt and a little rice flour for crispness if needed.
Spread thin on a tawa immediately (no fermentation).
Cook with oil until crisp; serve with ginger chutney.

name: Appam
steps: Grind soaked rice and cooked rice into a smooth batter.
Ferment overnight; add coconut milk and salt before cooking.
Pour in an appam pan, swirl to coat edges, and cover.
Remove once center is spongy and edges are lacey.

name: Sambar Idli
steps: Prepare a thin, spicy sambar with tamarind and dal.
Place 10-12 mini idlis in a deep bowl.
Pour hot sambar until idlis are fully submerged.
Top with a spoon of ghee and coriander; let soak for 2 mins.

name: Arachuvitta Sambar
steps: Boil dal and vegetables separately until soft.
Roast and grind coconut with spices into a fresh paste.
Simmer tamarind water with salt and vegetables; stir in dal and paste.
Temper with mustard seeds and hing in gingelly oil.

name: Pepper Rasam
steps: Coarsely crush pepper, cumin, and garlic.
Simmer tamarind water with tomato, salt, and crushed spices.
Turn off heat as soon as it froths; do not boil.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee.

name: Vatha Kuzhambu
steps: Fry dried berries (vathal) in thick gingelly oil and set aside.
Sauté shallots and garlic; add thick tamarind extract and spices.
Simmer until the gravy thickens and oil floats on top.
Mix in the fried berries and a tiny piece of jaggery.

name: Carrot Beans Poriyal
steps: Temper mustard seeds, urad dal, and green chillies.
Add finely chopped vegetables and salt; steam with minimal water.
Once water evaporates and veggies are tender, add grated coconut.
Toss and remove from heat immediately.

name: Keerai Kootu
steps: Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric until mushy.
Add chopped spinach and salt; cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in a paste of coconut and cumin.
Temper with mustard and urad dal in coconut oil.

name: Meen Kuzhambu
steps: Sauté shallots and garlic in gingelly oil with fenugreek seeds.
Add tamarind juice, chilli powder, and coriander powder; boil well.
Gently slide in fish pieces and simmer for 7 minutes.
Rest for at least 1 hour to let the fish absorb the tang.

name: Urulaikizhangu Varuval
steps: Boil potatoes, peel, and cube them.
Heat oil, temper with fennel and crushed garlic.
Add potatoes, sambar powder, and salt.
Roast on low flame until the exterior is dark and crispy.

name: Chicken Chettinad
steps: Dry roast and grind pepper, fennel, and cinnamon spices.
Sauté shallots, ginger-garlic, and tomatoes in oil.
Add chicken and the ground masala; sauté until oil separates.
Finish with a heavy garnish of fresh curry leaves.

name: Lemon Rice
steps: Temper mustard, urad dal, peanuts, and dry chillies in oil.
Add turmeric and curry leaves; turn off the heat.
Add lemon juice and salt to the tempering.
Pour over cooled cooked rice and mix gently.

name: Curd Rice (Thayir Sadam)
steps: Overcook rice until very soft and mash it while hot.
Mix with milk and curd once cooled to prevent souring.
Temper with mustard, ginger, green chillies, and curry leaves.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds or grated carrot.

name: Mutton Chukka
steps: Pressure cook mutton with ginger-garlic paste until tender.
Sauté a large amount of shallots and curry leaves in oil.
Add cooked mutton and a lot of crushed black pepper.
Fry on high heat until the meat is dry and coated in spices.

name: Cabbage Kootu
steps: Boil chana dal and chopped cabbage with turmeric until soft.
Add coconut-cumin paste and salt; simmer for 5 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds and urad dal.
Serve as a side dish for Sambar or Rasam.

name: Vazhakkai Podimas
steps: Boil raw banana with skin, then peel and grate it.
Temper mustard, urad dal, green chillies, and ginger.
Sauté the grated banana with salt and turmeric.
Garnish with grated coconut and curry leaves.

name: Tomato Thokku
steps: Finely chop or puree tomatoes.
Heat oil; temper mustard seeds and hing.
Cook tomatoes with salt and chilli powder on low heat.
Simmer until the water evaporates and oil leaves the sides.

name: Paruppu Urundai Kuzhambu
steps: Grind soaked dals with chillies; steam into small dumplings.
Prepare a thin tamarind-based spicy gravy (Puli Kuzhambu).
Gently add the steamed dumplings into the boiling gravy.
Simmer until the dumplings absorb the juice and float.

name: Egg Thokku
steps: Sauté onions and ginger-garlic paste until brown.
Add tomatoes, fennel powder, and salt; cook until mushy.
Slit boiled eggs and add to the masala.
Roast for 5 minutes until the eggs are well coated.

name: Kovakkai Fry
steps: Thinly slice ivy gourd into rounds.
Temper mustard seeds; add gourd, turmeric, and salt.
Stir in sambar powder and roast on low flame.
Cook until the gourd is shrunk and slightly charred/crispy.

name: Bisi Bele Bath (TN Style)
steps: Pressure cook rice, dal, and vegetables together with turmeric.
Add tamarind extract and the ground spice masala.
Simmer until the consistency is gooey and well-blended.
Temper with plenty of ghee, cashews, and mustard seeds.

name: Puliyodarai (Tamarind Rice)
steps: Cook rice grains and spread to cool; mix with gingelly oil.
Cook tamarind pulp with spices until it becomes a thick paste (Pulikachal).
Temper mustard, chana dal, peanuts, and dry chillies.
Mix the paste and tempering into the cooled rice.

name: Thuvayal (Thengai)
steps: Roast urad dal and red chillies until golden brown.
Grind with coconut, tamarind, ginger, and salt.
Add very little water to keep the texture thick and coarse.
Serve as a side for rice and pepper rasam.

name: Kathirikai Gotsu
steps: Mash boiled brinjal and a small amount of moong dal.
Sauté onions and tomatoes; add tamarind water and salt.
Mix in the mashed brinjal and simmer for 10 minutes.
Serve as an accompaniment for Pongal or Rice.

name: Mor Kuzhambu
steps: Grind coconut, ginger, and chillies into a smooth paste.
Whisk curd with the paste, salt, and turmeric.
Heat gently on low flame; remove before it boils (to prevent curdling).
Temper with mustard seeds and fenugreek.

name: Soya Chunks Varuval
steps: Boil soya chunks, squeeze out water, and set aside.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and curry leaves.
Add soya, fennel powder, and chilli powder.
Roast on medium flame until the spices coat the chunks.

name: Beetroot Oru-pattu
steps: Cook grated beetroot and moong dal together until soft.
Add a coarse grind of coconut and cumin.
Stir for 2 minutes and temper with mustard seeds.
Serve as a healthy, sweet-savory side dish.

name: Pudalangai (Snake Gourd) Kootu
steps: Pressure cook sliced gourd and chana dal with turmeric.
Add coconut and chilli paste with salt.
Simmer for 5 minutes until flavors blend.
Temper with mustard and urad dal in coconut oil.

name: Masala Vadai
steps: Coarsely grind soaked chana dal with red chillies and fennel.
Mix in chopped shallots, salt, and curry leaves.
Flatten small portions into discs.
Deep fry on medium flame until dark golden and crunchy.

name: Kai Murukku
steps: Mix flours, butter, cumin, and hing into a stiff dough.
Hand-twist the dough into concentric circles (spirals).
Deep fry until the oil bubbles subside.
Drain and store once cooled for a signature crunch.

name: Ribbon Pakoda
steps: Combine flours, butter, salt, and chilli powder.
Use the flat-slit disc in a murukku press.
Press directly into hot oil in a circular motion.
Fry until crisp and break into strips.

name: Sundal (Chickpea)
steps: Pressure cook soaked chickpeas until tender.
Temper mustard, chillies, and curry leaves in oil.
Toss the chickpeas with salt and the tempering.
Finish with a generous amount of fresh grated coconut.

name: Bajji (Onion/Potato)
steps: Make a thick batter of flours, spices, and a pinch of soda.
Dip thin slices of onion or potato into the batter.
Deep fry until the coating puffs up and turns golden.
Serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Keerai Vadai
steps: Grind urad dal to a thick paste as for Medhu Vadai.
Mix in finely chopped spinach, onions, and chillies.
Shape into discs and deep fry.
The spinach adds a unique earthy flavor and extra crunch.

name: Vazhakkai Bajji
steps: Peel and slice raw banana into long, thin strips.
Dip in spiced gram flour batter.
Deep fry until crisp.
This is a staple 'tea-shop' snack in Tamil Nadu.

name: Thattai
steps: Mix rice flour with ground fried gram and soaked chana dal.
Add spices and curry leaves; form a stiff dough.
Flatten into thin, small discs on a greased plastic sheet.
Deep fry on low heat until golden and very brittle.

name: Kara Boondi
steps: Make a smooth batter and pour through a perforated ladle into oil.
Fry the tiny balls until crisp; drain.
Mix with fried peanuts, curry leaves, and crushed fried garlic.
Toss with salt and chilli powder while warm.

name: Sweet Paniyaram
steps: Mix idli batter with melted jaggery and cardamom powder.
Add small fried coconut bits for texture.
Pour into a paniyaram pan greased with ghee.
Cook until the exterior is dark brown and the center is soft.

name: Mysore Pak (Soft)
steps: Sieve besan and mix with a little ghee to avoid lumps.
Boil sugar to a single-string consistency.
Add besan and keep stirring while pouring hot ghee continuously.
Once it becomes a smooth, non-sticky mass, set in a tray.

name: Omapodi
steps: Soak ajwain in water, grind, and filter the water.
Knead flours with ajwain water and butter.
Press through the finest hole disc of a murukku maker into oil.
Fry for just a minute until the color is pale yellow.

name: Pori Urundai
steps: Prepare a thick jaggery syrup (hard ball consistency).
Add ginger powder and cardamom.
Quickly pour syrup over puffed rice and mix.
Grease palms and roll into tight balls before it cools.

name: Aval Mixture
steps: Deep fry thick poha in small batches until it puffs.
Fry peanuts, cashews, and curry leaves separately.
Toss everything together with salt, chilli powder, and turmeric.
This is a light, crunchy tea-time favorite.

name: Boli (Sweet)
steps: Make a soft, oily dough with maida and turmeric.
Stuff with a sweet paste of boiled chana dal and jaggery (Puran).
Roll into thin discs and cook on a tawa with ghee.
Serve warm.

name: Kallu Urundai
steps: Powder sugar and fried gram (pottukadalai) separately.
Mix the powders with cardamom.
Pour hot, melted ghee over the mix until it can be bound.
Shape into round balls that melt in the mouth.

name: Rava Laddu
steps: Roast rava in ghee until aromatic and grind to a fine powder.
Mix with powdered sugar and ghee-fried nuts.
Add warm ghee gradually and roll into balls.
Use a little milk for binding if you plan to consume it fast.

name: Sukhiyan
steps: Boil green gram and mix with jaggery and coconut bits.
Shape into small balls.
Dip the balls into a thin maida-turmeric batter.
Deep fry until the outer layer is crisp.

name: Adhirasam
steps: Soak rice, dry slightly, and grind into a moist flour.
Make a specific 'soft-string' jaggery syrup.
Mix flour into syrup and rest the dough for 2-3 days.
Pat into discs and deep fry on low heat.

name: Seeval
steps: Mix flours with a paste of garlic and chillies.
Use the 'ribbon' disc in the press.
Fry until the garlic aroma is strong and the seeval is crisp.
Commonly found in the Tirunelveli region.

name: Paal Bun
steps: Knead maida with curd and a pinch of soda into a soft dough.
Ferment for 2 hours.
Deep fry small lemon-sized balls of dough.
Immediately drop into warm sugar syrup for 5 minutes.

name: Thenkuzhal
steps: Use a 4:1 ratio of rice to urad dal flour.
Knead with butter, cumin, and salt.
Press through the 3-hole disc into hot oil.
Fry until it turns creamy white and stops bubbling.

name: Masala Peanuts
steps: Coat peanuts with flours, spices, and ginger-garlic paste.
Sprinkle very little water to make the coating stick.
Deep fry until the peanuts are crunchy and the shell is hard.
Toss with extra curry leaves.

name: Wheat Halwa (Tirunelveli Style)
steps: Soak wheat, grind, and extract 'milk'.
Ferment the milk overnight, then discard the top water.
Cook the thick milk with sugar and plenty of ghee.
Stir for hours until it becomes a translucent, jelly-like mass.

name: Malabar Parotta (TN Style)
steps: Knead a soft, stretchy dough and rest for 2 hours with oil.
Roll thin, pleat like a fan, and coil into a spiral.
Flatten and toast on a tawa with oil until golden layers appear.
Crush the parotta with both hands while hot to separate layers.

name: Vegetable Salna
steps: Grind coconut, poppy seeds, and fennel into a very smooth paste.
Sauté onions, tomatoes, and kalpasi (stone flower) for aroma.
Add vegetables and ground paste; simmer until a thin, oily gravy forms.
Serve as the essential pairing for Parotta.

name: Kothu Parotta
steps: Shred cooked parottas into small bits.
Sauté onions and chillies; scramble eggs into the mix.
Add the shredded parotta and a generous amount of Salna.
Beat vigorously with a heavy spatula on a hot tawa until blended.

name: Idiyappam & Coconut Milk
steps: Press rice flour dough through a mold and steam for 5 minutes.
Extract thick milk from fresh grated coconut.
Sweeten the milk with jaggery and flavor with cardamom.
Serve idiyappam submerged in the sweet coconut milk.

name: Egg Veechu Dosa
steps: Stretch dough/batter very thin over a large square tawa.
Crack an egg in the center and spread it to the edges.
Fold the four sides inward to create a square envelope.
Flip and cook until the egg inside is set and the outside is crisp.

name: Puttu (Rice)
steps: Moisten rice flour with salt water until it reaches a crumbly texture.
Layer flour and coconut in a puttu steamer (cylindrical).
Steam for 8-10 minutes until a distinct aroma arises.
Serve with Kadala (Chickpea) curry or banana and sugar.

name: Tomato Sevai
steps: Prepare or steam rice sevai and keep it fluffy.
Sauté onions and tomatoes with turmeric until mushy.
Toss the sevai gently into the tomato base.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

name: Arisi Upma
steps: Coarsely grind rice and dal (like rava/grits).
Temper mustard, red chillies, and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Add water (1:2 ratio) and bring to a boil; stir in the rice grits.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles until fluffy.

name: Vegetable Kurma
steps: Grind coconut, cashews, and fennel into a rich paste.
Sauté whole spices and vegetables in a pressure cooker.
Add the paste and water; cook for 1 whistle.
Perfect side for Chapatis or Idiyappam.

name: Godhumai (Wheat) Rava Upma
steps: Temper mustard and dals; sauté onions and ginger.
Add 2.5 cups of water for 1 cup of wheat rava and salt.
Add rava to boiling water and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Serve with coconut chutney; a healthy diabetic-friendly dinner.

name: Podi Dosa
steps: Spread dosa batter thinly on a hot tawa.
Sprinkle a generous amount of spicy idli podi over the top.
Drizzle gingelly oil and cook until the podi crisps up.
Fold and serve without flipping.

name: Muttai (Egg) Ceylon Parotta
steps: Roll parotta dough into a very thin square.
Spread a mixture of beaten egg and cooked minced meat in the center.
Fold into a square and shallow fry on a tawa with oil.
Slice into rectangles and serve with salna.

name: Appam & Stew
steps: Make thin-edged, spongy-centered appams in a curved pan.
Simmer vegetables in thin coconut milk with ginger and pepper.
Add thick coconut milk at the end and turn off heat.
Do not boil after adding thick milk to prevent curdling.

name: Madurai Kari Dosai
steps: Spread a thick dosa; pour a beaten egg over it.
Top with a layer of spicy minced mutton (chukka).
Drizzle oil, flip carefully, and cook until the meat layer is seared.
A famous Madurai street food specialty.

name: Milagu Jeera Kanji
steps: Pressure cook rice and dal with garlic until very mushy (porridge).
Crush pepper and cumin coarsely and add to the kanji.
Stir in salt and a little coconut milk if desired.
Light dinner, perfect for rainy days or recovery.

name: Keema (Minced Meat) Dosa
steps: Sauté minced meat with onions and spices until dry.
Spread dosa batter; place the keema in the center.
Fold the dosa and press lightly to set.
Serve with a spicy gravy.

name: Varagu (Millet) Arisi Sambar Sadam
steps: Cook millet and dal together until soft.
Add tamarind water, vegetables, and sambar powder.
Simmer until it reaches a mashy consistency.
Finish with a tempering of mustard and ghee-fried cashews.

name: Chapatis & Paneer Kurma
steps: Knead soft chapatis and puff them on a direct flame or tawa.
Make a white kurma base using coconut, chillies, and poppy seeds.
Add paneer cubes and simmer for 5 minutes.
A popular modern Tamil household dinner.

name: Ragi Semiya (Sweet/Salt)
steps: Rinse ragi semiya for 2 minutes, drain, and steam for 5 minutes.
For sweet: Toss with grated coconut, sugar, and cardamom.
For salt: Temper with mustard, chillies, and onions.
A very light and nutritious dinner option.

name: Eerul Pookkal (Onion Flower) Dosa
steps: Finely chop a large amount of shallots (small onions).
Sauté them slightly and mix into the dosa batter.
Make thick, soft dosas (Uttapam style).
Serve with spicy garlic chutney.

name: Kal Dosa & Vadacurry
steps: Make 'Kal Dosa' (slightly thick, soft dosas).
Prepare Vadacurry by crumbling fried lentil fritters into a spicy gravy.
The gravy should be thick and flavorful with fennel and cloves.
A classic Chennai-style dinner pairing.

name: Masala Macaroni (TN Style)
steps: Boil macaroni in salt water and drain.
Sauté onions, ginger-garlic, and tomatoes with TN spices.
Add fennel powder and chilli powder for a local twist.
Toss macaroni in the masala and finish with coriander.

name: Thinai (Foxtail Millet) Pongal
steps: Pressure cook millet and dal (1:4 water ratio) until very soft.
Temper ghee with crushed pepper, cumin, ginger, and curry leaves.
Fold the tempering into the pongal.
Lighter on the stomach than rice pongal for dinner.

name: Pichu Poota Chicken (Shredded) Dosa
steps: Sauté shredded chicken with lots of black pepper and onions.
Spread dosa batter; layer the pepper chicken on top.
Press down and cook with oil until crisp.
Serve with a simple chicken gravy (Saaru).

name: Bread Upma
steps: Toast bread slices and cut into small cubes.
Temper mustard and urad dal; sauté onions and tomatoes with spices.
Add a splash of water to make the masala slightly damp.
Toss the bread cubes until coated and serve immediately.
